propositions: A 106-line CAS push loop in reconcile-bridge.yml duplicates logic in push.py with divergent retry budgets (5 vs 3), missing final-push fix, and conflicting defect resolutions
The YAML loop and canary loop carry standing-decision blocks that explicitly forbid extraction; these decisions must be explicitly overturned rather than bypassed

Strict mode must fail loud on every silent best-effort return path (non-retriable decline, rebase/merge-recovery guard, store-epoch guard, merge-clean-then-exhausted, lock timeout) and emit no BRIDGE_ALERT event per decision D1
A new core entrypoint must stage+commit a dirty tracker tree before pushing, preserving the reconciler's commit-back while keeping push.py pure push-only
Strict mode must be applied at the call site (reconciler strict, canary best-effort, library default best-effort) with strict treating sync.push=off/async as configuration contradictions
The commit-back identity must be passed explicitly into the core entrypoint and applied per-commit via git -c flags to preserve authorship when moved from workflow shell context
